Singapore expands haze inquiries to 10 locally based firms
article:
Singapore expanded its investigation into haze-creating fires in Indonesia that have blanketed the city-state in smog, requesting information from 10 locally registered companies.

The National Environment Agency sent notices seeking documents and details of land concessions in Indonesia owned by the firms, their fire-fighting and blaze prevention measures, and their relationship to other relevant companies, according to a Friday statement.

All 10 Singapore-registered companies are involved in the palm oil or forestry sectors and include Wilmar International, Golden Agri International, and First Resources the agency said.

Singapore, Malaysia and other parts of Southeast Asia have experienced some of the worst pollution since 2015 as a result of haze generated by blazes in Indonesia. While fires are typical every year, the issue has been exacerbated in recent months as drought conditions have been worsened by a record El Niño.

Wilmar, the world’s biggest palm oil refiner, said in a statement that “work is in progress to comply,” with the NEA notice. First Resources is “reviewing the notice and will provide the requested documents and information,” it said Saturday.

Golden Agri, which operates oil palm assets across Sumatra, Kalimantan and Papua, has received the request and will cooperate with the agency to provide information, the company said in a stock exchange filing late Saturday. The producer said earlier this month that it wasn’t aware of information indicating its operations had contributed to the haze, and that it had stepped up fire-prevention measures ahead of the El Niño-driven drought.

See also: Singapore issues haze notices to three more Indonesian firms

The NEA earlier issued requests for information to 10 Indonesia-registered companies in connection with the haze.

Singapore’s Prime Minister Lawrence Wong has pledged to investigate companies behind the region-wide smog and to take legal action under the Transboundary Haze Act. The law gives Singapore the ability to fine companies up to S$100,000 ($78,000) per day of pollution. However, the city-state has yet to issue any penalties under the legislation.

A panel of experts including law firms, auditors and investigative companies with expertise in cross-border inquiries will support the government’s efforts, the law ministry said Friday in a statement.

See also: RegCo queries SGX-listed Indonesian agri firms on cause and impact of haze

“The conduct of local and foreign companies, their corporate relationships and supply chains, will be examined to establish whether they have been involved in causing or condoning the fires that caused or contributed to the haze,” the ministry said.

Some palm oil producers have previously denied that their operations in Indonesia have caused or contributed to the pollution, pointing to strict zero-burning policies.

Air quality in Singapore improved Sunday, with the city-state’s preferred gauge — the 24-hour PSI — ranging from 102 to 135 as of 9 a.m. local time, levels considered to be “unhealthy.” Readings of 201 or more are considered “very unhealthy” and levels above 301 are regarded as “hazardous” and can trigger school closures.

title: IndiGo, Air India to shift some flights to new Mumbai airport
article:
(Oct 25): IndiGo and Air India will move some of its international operations to Navi Mumbai International Airport as two of India’s biggest airlines expand their presence at the new aviation facility serving the country’s financial capital.

IndiGo announced the move in a joint statement with airport operator Adani Airport Holdings Ltd on Sunday, saying it will “progressively transfer” 12 daily international departures from Mumbai’s Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj International Airport (CSMIA) to the newly opened facility starting February 2027. The shift will include all existing IndiGo services from Mumbai to Bahrain, Riyadh, Dammam, Jeddah, Madinah, Kuwait, Ras Al Khaimah, Fujairah, Muscat, Dhaka and Jakarta, as well as a planned daily service to Kathmandu.

Air India Group will gradually shift some flights to the Middle East from January, with the transition expected to be completed by the 2027 summer schedule. Some services are subject to regulatory approvals. Its subsidiary Air India Express will begin four daily domestic flights from December 2026.

The shift comes as Mumbai International Airport prepares to redevelop its aging Terminal 1, requiring traffic to be redistributed between Mumbai’s two airports. Airlines had earlier resisted efforts to move flights from Mumbai’s CSMIA to the Navi Mumbai airport but with the Adani Group controlling both airports, the reallocation underscores its influence over how air traffic is distributed across India’s financial capital.

“The phased transition is intended to support a transparent, equitable and proportionate rebalancing of capacity across Mumbai’s dual airport system, taking into account each airline’s presence at CSMIA,” the joint release said.

Adani Airport, controlled by billionaire Gautam Adani, is India’s largest private-sector airport operator, managing eight airports across seven cities and planning an US$11 billion investment to bid for a dozen more terminals by 2030.

See also: VietJet faces aircraft, cash seizures in FitzWalter debt fight

title: Chinese manufacturer Dongshan raises US$1.3 bil in HK listing
article:
(Oct 25): Suzhou Dongshan Precision Manufacturing Co, a printed circuit board maker, raised about HK$9.9 billion (US$1.3 billion) in Hong Kong’s biggest listing in nearly two months, which hit a volatile market for companies related to the artificial intelligence build out.

The company priced its shares at HK$86.80 apiece, compared to a maximum of HK$93.80, according to a filing to the city’s stock exchange on Sunday, which confirmed an earlier Bloomberg News report.

Dongshan Precision said it had not exercised an option to upsize the deal, meaning it sold about 113.8 million shares in the offering. Trading is expected to begin on Oct 28.

Dongshan Precision’s Shenzhen-listed stock is up 35% this year even after a nearly 60% slide from a June peak.

Dongshan Precision, which makes the components that tare the intricate electronic backbone of AI servers, is braving the market at a tricky time across Asia especially for companies in its business.

See also: Brookfield to open Doha office to deepen its Middle East reach

First-time listings have raised more than US$50 billion in Hong Kong this year, edging closer to the US$57.8 billion record set in 2010, but rising bond yields and poor deal performance are making investors and issuers more cautious.

A string of withdrawals and delays, including by major data centre operators in the region, has prompted some companies to put near-term listing plans on hold.

“With Dongshan’s Shenzhen share price declining substantially, the reference valuation for its Hong Kong offering has also fallen,” said Francis Tan, Asia chief strategist at Indosuez Wealth Management in Singapore. “Investors still want exposure to the AI revolution, but they are increasingly demanding earnings visibility rather than simply buying the narrative.”

See also: Goldman cuts Kospi 12-month target by 25% as AI trade unravels

Chinese technology stocks have been particularly hit hard, with no end in sight for a deepening selloff as investors confront the realities of an economy that’s weak enough to erode corporate profits but not to trigger forceful new stimulus.

The world’s second-largest equities market has lost US$3.5 trillion in value from a peak in May, data compiled by Bloomberg show. The rout intensified last week, pushing the onshore benchmark CSI 300 Index into a bear market and a technology sector gauge in Hong Kong towards erasing all of its gains since Beijing’s sweeping growth support package two years ago.

Dongshan Precision’s listing leaned heavily on cornerstone investors, which get guaranteed allocation in the deal in exchange for holding the stock for at least six months. They include JPMorgan Asset Management, Alibaba Group Holding Ltd, CPE and Montage Technology Co, who agreed to buy a combined 50% of the offering. Jane Street Group and Jump Trading LLC are also among them.

The Suzhou-based company makes PCBs and optical transceivers, key components for AI. It’s the third-largest PCB supplier in an US$85.2 billion global market, according to its prospectus.

UBS Group AG, Guotai Haitong Securities Co, GF Securities Co and Citic Securities Co are joint sponsors for the Hong Kong listing.

title: Brookfield to open Doha office to deepen its Middle East reach
article:
(Oct 25): Brookfield Asset Management Ltd is opening an office in Qatar, deepening its presence in the Middle East where many countries are grappling with the economic fallout from the war.

The office will be anchored by Brookfield’s global credit platform, including Oaktree, the firm said in a statement on Sunday.

The move builds on its partnership with Qai, Qatar’s artificial intelligence company and a subsidiary of the Qatar Investment Authority (QIA), to invest US$20 billion in artificial intelligence infrastructure in Qatar and international markets. Brookfield manages about US$20 billion in assets across private equity, real estate, credit and infrastructure across the six-nation Gulf Cooperation Council.

“Establishing our presence in Doha is a natural next step as we continue to grow our business in the region,” said Jad Ellawn, Brookfield’s managing partner and regional head of the Middle East. “We see significant opportunity ahead and look forward to continuing to invest and deepen our collaborations here for the long term.”

The expansion is the latest sign of global giants doubling down on the Middle East, which is home to sovereign wealth funds that oversee assets worth trillions of dollars. These investors have become increasingly crucial to financial firms, who’ve been keen to signal their willingness to back Gulf countries during the conflict.

In recent days, Advent International, Eurazeo, EQT AB and Pantheon have opened offices in Abu Dhabi, while Robinhood Markets Inc plans to launch its retail investing platform in the Middle East from a new Dubai base next year.

See also: Goldman cuts Kospi 12-month target by 25% as AI trade unravels

Before the conflict began, the QIA had been signalling a return to the large transactions that helped establish it as one of the world’s biggest sovereign investors. That prompted firms including BlackRock Inc’s Global Infrastructure Partners to establish offices in Doha.

Now, Qatar’s energy sales have taken a major hit. An Iranian strike on Ras Laffan in March knocked out about 17% of the country’s liquefied natural gas (LNG) export capacity, with losses estimated at US$20 billion and repairs expected to take at least three years. LNG shipments remain well below prewar levels amid risks to tanker traffic through the Strait of Hormuz.

Still, the QIA has continued to pursue global deals and partnerships. In September, it said it was targeting a US$20 billion partnership with JPMorgan Chase & Co, following a similar agreement with Goldman Sachs Group Inc.

title: Goldman cuts Kospi 12-month target by 25% as AI trade unravels
article:
(Oct 25): Goldman Sachs Group Inc strategists slashed their target for South Korea’s Kospi Index by 25%, after raising it repeatedly this year, as concerns over the artificial intelligence trade intensify.

The analysts including Timothy Moe lowered their 12-month target for Korea’s equity gauge to 9,000 from 12,000, citing more conservative valuation assumptions after the benchmark plunged more than 35% from its June peak. The selloff has left the equities highly undervalued, according to the strategists, and the revised forecast still implies a more than 60% upside from current levels.

Goldman analysts most recently raised their target for the Kospi in June, and had maintained it at 12,000 even as the index’s stocks slumped in a global AI selloff that started later that month.

Chipmaking giants including Samsung Electronics Co and SK Hynix Inc have made the Kospi a bellwether for the AI trade. The index has suffered from investors’ growing concern about the sustainability of massive infrastructure spending and rising financing costs in the sector, with little sign of sufficient returns. The selling pressure has spilled into the broader Korean market.

“The market is pricing an overly negative fundamental outlook,” the Goldman strategists wrote in a note dated Oct 25. The target was lowered “to incorporate more conservative assumptions about how the market may price underlying fundamentals but still view the market as offering attractive risk/reward at current levels,” they added.

South Korea has transformed from the year’s hottest major market into the world’s cheapest, with valuations falling to roughly half of Indonesia’s. The Kospi’s 12-month forward price-to-earnings ratio has fallen to about four, a valuation last seen in 2006 across any of the 18 markets, after starting 2026 with a value over US$1 trillion, according to data compiled by Bloomberg.

See also: Britain’s migration clampdown puts fear into £15 bil care sector

The Goldman strategists estimate that current semiconductor valuations imply a 65% decline in the sector’s 2027 earnings, a scenario it considers excessively pessimistic. Stocks outside the memory sector, which account for about half the index, trade at 7.6 times forward earnings.

Despite the latest cut, the bank continues to favour opportunities in power, industrials, corporate governance-related stocks and companies benefitting from domestic reflation and Korean popular culture.
